slices.slice: Browser rendering of Gaussian splats and splat file formats, mid-2026 state — Spark, PlayCanvas SuperSplat/SOG, mkkellogg GaussianSplats3D, Babylon.js, splat-transform, camera-path authoring
slices.summary: The mid-2026 web-splat stack has consolidated hard around PlayCanvas's tooling and Spark's renderer, with the old antimatter15-lineage (.splat, mkkellogg/GaussianSplats3D) explicitly deprecated by its own maintainer in favor of Spark. Format-wise, PlayCanvas's SOG (Spatially-Ordered Gaussians, announced Sept 2025, "the WebP of Gaussian Splatting") has become the de facto browser-delivery format: WebP-textured, Morton-ordered, GPU-decode-ready, cutting a 1GB PLY to 42MB. It's natively supported by Spark (since late 2025) and Babylon.js v9 (March 26, 2026), and is produced by PlayCanvas's open-source splat-transform CLI, which now reads/writes PLY, SOG, Streamed SOG, SPZ, SPLAT, KSPLAT, GLB, and even bakes voxel-collision octrees and standalone HTML viewers. Niantic Spatial's SPZ format shipped v4 (May 5, 2026) with 3-5x faster encoding, an uncapped point count, and SH degree-4 support, and sits at the center of Khronos's new KHR_gaussian_splatting glTF extension (release-candidate Feb 3, 2026, ratification expected Q2 2026) — making SPZ the better long-term interchange bet even though SOG currently wins for raw in-browser decode. Spark (sparkjs.dev, MIT, World Labs) shipped a major v2.0 (April 2026) LOD "splat tree" for 100M+ splat worlds and v2.1 (May 2026), remains WebGL2-only, and has no built-in keyframe timeline — that job now belongs to PlayCanvas SuperSplat, whose Timeline panel (v2.0, Feb 2025) can auto-seed camera keyframes from COLMAP poses and, as of v2.2, renders fly-through MP4s locally in-browser with zero upload. Babylon.js v9 added splat shadows, native SOG loading, and experimental sort-free "Triangle Splatting."

sources.title: SparkRenderer docs - Spark
key_claims: SparkRenderer requires a THREE.WebGLRenderer (WebGL2) instance and disables antialiasing since it doesn't help splat rendering; no WebGPU path documented
Offers radial vs Z-depth splat sorting and configurable target splat counts: ~500K-750K for WebXR, 1-1.5M mobile, 2.5M desktop via lodSplatScale

recommendations: Standardize the shipped web-viewer artifact on PlayCanvas's .sog (Spatially-Ordered Gaussians) format instead of the current ad-hoc 'artifact.splat' — SOG is Morton-ordered WebP-backed data that decodes GPU-ready with no per-splat CPU unpack, is natively supported by Spark (since v0.1.6, SOGSv2 since v0.1.10) and Babylon.js v9, and PlayCanvas's own showcase shrinks a 1GB PLY to 42MB (~95% smaller) at 4M gaussians — 2-3x better than compressed PLY.

Keep .ply (or compressed .ply) as the archival/master format straight out of gsplat/Brush training, and insert one conversion step using the open-source @playcanvas/splat-transform CLI (Node) to filter NaN/floaters, Morton-reorder, and emit both the archive PLY and a Streamed SOG (auto-LOD'd if the bridge+roadway scene exceeds 1M gaussians) for the web bundle. This replaces any hand-rolled format-writing code.

Do not add WebGPU or switch renderers: Spark (sparkjs.dev, MIT, backed by World Labs) is WebGL2-only but actively developed (v2.1.0 May 18 2026, v2.0.0 April 14 2026 added an LOD splat tree for 100M-1B+ splat scenes), and is exactly what mkkellogg explicitly tells GaussianSplats3D users to migrate to since his repo 'is no longer in active development' (last release v0.4.7, Jan 2025). Orbit Studio's existing Spark/three.js viewer choice is already the right one — just feed it .sog instead of raw .splat.

For keyframed fly-through camera paths, do not build a custom timeline UI in Orbit Studio's own viewer. Instead route trained scenes through the free, open-source SuperSplat editor (superspl.at/editor): its Timeline panel can import the COLMAP camera poses Orbit Studio already computes via pycolmap to auto-seed keyframes matching the real capture path, then let the user hand-adjust and use SuperSplat 2.2's local, no-upload Render menu to export an MP4 fly-through directly in-browser.

For the interactive (non-video) fly-through experience, export the SuperSplat-authored keyframe/path data and drive it through a thin custom THREE.Camera interpolator inside the existing Spark viewer — Spark is explicitly camera-control-agnostic ('any camera control scheme compatible with THREE.js'), so this is a small integration, not a new subsystem.

Add Niantic's SPZ (Apache-2.0 OR MIT, github.com/nianticlabs/spz) only as a secondary/interchange export — not the primary web format — for users who want to pull the bridge scene into other engines (Unity, robotics, etc.); SPZ 4 (May 5 2026) is 3-5x faster to encode and now uncaps the old 10M-point limit, and it's the format named in Khronos's KHR_gaussian_splatting glTF extension (release candidate Feb 3, 2026) contributor list, so it's the better long-term portability bet even though SOG currently wins for raw browser decode speed.

Flag to the user that KHR_gaussian_splatting (glTF 2.0 Gaussian-splat extension, backed by Autodesk/Bentley-Cesium/Esri/Huawei/Niantic Spatial/NVIDIA) is still pre-ratification as of this research (release candidate Feb 2026, ratification 'expected Q2 2026' — actual ratification date unconfirmed) — worth revisiting in a few months but not yet something to build against.
uncertainties: Whether KHR_gaussian_splatting has actually been ratified by Khronos as of today (July 23, 2026) — only a Feb 3, 2026 release-candidate announcement with ratification 'expected Q2 2026' was confirmed; no ratification-complete announcement was found.
Whether Spark has shipped any release beyond v2.1.0 (May 18, 2026) between then and July 23, 2026 — the releases page fetch may not reflect the very latest tag.
Whether Spark has added or roadmapped WebGPU support — current docs describe a WebGL2-only renderer with no WebGPU path mentioned either way.
Exact mechanism SuperSplat 2.2 uses for local video export (e.g., WebCodecs vs MediaRecorder) was not confirmed from source text.
Whether Babylon.js's native SOG loader and Spark's SOG loader are cross-compatible with the exact same .sog files (both claim SOG/SOGS support but interop wasn't independently verified).
Whether splat-transform's 'HTML Viewer' export target uses Spark, PlayCanvas engine, or another renderer under the hood — not stated in the fetched README excerpt.

recommendations: Keep the ffmpeg equirect-to-perspective reframe stage: none of the production-ready feed-forward models (VGGT, VGGT-Omega, Pi3/Pi3X, MapAnything, AnySplat, Depth Anything 3) ingest equirectangular panoramas natively -- all expect perspective crops. Feed each of the 20 panoramas as ~6-8 cube-face crops (~120-160 perspective images) into the feed-forward model.

Replace the pycolmap/COLMAP SfM stage with MapAnything (facebookresearch/map-anything, v1.1.3, 2026-07-17) using the Apache-2.0 'facebook/map-anything-apache' checkpoint (not the default CC-BY-NC checkpoint). It wraps VGGT/DUSt3R/MASt3R/Pi3-X interchangeably, handles far more views than you need (2000-view mode documented), and exports directly to COLMAP cameras/images/points3D format -- which Brush (already vendored) already reads natively, so no downstream code changes are needed.

Do not drop per-scene splat training. Feed MapAnything's poses + metric point cloud into Brush/gsplat as initialization instead of running COLMAP feature matching + bundle adjustment -- this removes the slowest, most failure-prone part of the Colab T4 pipeline (matching wide-baseline, low-overlap bridge shots) while keeping training quality from real optimization.

Add AnySplat (MIT license, InternRobotics/AnySplat, SIGGRAPH Asia 2025) as an optional instant-preview path: same perspective crops -> direct feed-forward Gaussian splat output in seconds, useful for on-site/Colab-free sanity checks before committing to a full training run. It is not a proven substitute for the final bridge-scale scene yet.

Do not add SPAG4d to the pipeline for this use case -- it is single-panorama monocular projection (no multi-view fusion across your 20 photos), and its higher-quality backends (PaGeR, SHARP 360) plus the OmniRoam refinement path are research-only/Adobe-Research-License, which conflicts with an open pipeline.

Avoid anchoring the pipeline on DUSt3R, MASt3R, or Pi3/Pi3X weights, or the default VGGT-1B checkpoint -- all are CC BY-NC(-SA) 4.0, non-commercial only. If VGGT is used instead of MapAnything, use the VGGT-1B-Commercial checkpoint specifically.

Track PanoVGGT, VGGT-360, and 360-GeoGS as a future upgrade path -- they are purpose-built for exactly this scenario (sets of 2-24 outdoor equirectangular panoramas -> poses/depth/points in one pass, PanoVGGT reports strong urban outdoor pose/depth accuracy) and would eliminate the perspective-reframe step entirely, but as of 2026-07-23 their code/weights release could not be confirmed live (papers say 'code and dataset will be released'). Revisit in Q4 2026.
slices.slice: Feed-forward / pose-free 3D reconstruction models (DUSt3R/MASt3R lineage, VGGT/VGGT-Omega, Pi3/Pi3X, MapAnything, AnySplat, SPAG4d, Depth Anything 3, panorama-native successors)
slices.summary: The feed-forward/pose-free reconstruction field matured fast in H1 2026. VGGT (CVPR2025 Best Paper) got a commercial-licensed checkpoint (VGGT-1B-Commercial, 2025-07-29) and a successor, VGGT-Omega (CVPR2026 oral, gated weights), using 30% of VGGT's memory at 1.6x speed. Pi3/Pi3X (BSD-3 code, CC-BY-NC weights) is the fastest (57 FPS vs VGGT 43 FPS vs DUSt3R 1.25 FPS) and needs no reference view. Meta's MapAnything (Apache-2.0, v1.1.3, 2026-07-17) is the most pipeline-friendly: it wraps VGGT/DUSt3R/MASt3R/Pi3-X under one interface, scales to thousands of views, and exports straight to COLMAP format that Brush already consumes. AnySplat (MIT) and parts of Depth Anything 3 (Apache-2.0 base variants, 2025-11-14) go further, predicting Gaussians directly in one pass -- but only from perspective images. None of these ingest equirectangular panoramas natively. The real panorama-native successors -- PanoVGGT, VGGT-360, 360-GeoGS (all CVPR2026) -- are designed for exactly this task (multi-panorama outdoor sets) but their code release status is unconfirmed as of today. SPAG4d is a community tool (MIT core) that turns ONE equirectangular panorama into a splat via monocular depth, but does not fuse multiple wide-baseline panoramas, and its better backends carry non-commercial/Adobe licenses. Separately, COLMAP's own authors shipped GLUEMAP (CVPR2026), a hybrid pipeline that leans on feed-forward models (Pi3, SALAD, VGGSfM) specifically to patch COLMAP's classic failure modes: low texture, limited overlap, wide baseline -- exactly the profile of 20 sparse bridge photos. Net: feed-forward pose recovery can and should replace COLMAP's matching/SfM stage for a 20-image set today; fully replacing per-scene splat training is not yet proven at this scale.

Exact VRAM requirements for running VGGT, VGGT-Omega, or Pi3/Pi3X across ~120-160 perspective crops (from 20 panoramas x 6-8 faces) on a single Colab T4 were not documented in accessible sources -- only MapAnything's 2000-view/140GB figure was found, which is a datacenter-scale upper bound, not a T4-relevant lower bound.
Whether MapAnything's Apache-2.0 'facebook/map-anything-apache' checkpoint matches the reconstruction quality of the default CC-BY-NC checkpoint was not confirmed.
SPAG4d is a small community project (~215 GitHub stars at time of check); its production robustness and quality on real bridge/outdoor imagery beyond its own README claims is unverified.

Whether Splatter-360 and PanSplat (2025, code released) can fuse more than 2 wide-baseline panoramas into one persistent explorable scene, versus only pairwise novel-view synthesis, was not directly confirmed from the sources reached -- relevant if considering them as an alternative panorama-native path.
VGGT's exact 'commercial checkpoint' license text (VGGT-1B-Commercial) was described secondhand via search snippets, not fetched verbatim from Meta's own license file for that specific checkpoint.

recommendations: Do NOT replace the 20-photo COLMAP(pycolmap)+gsplat reconstruction with a from-scratch generative world model. The 20 registered panoramas already give genuine multi-view photogrammetric coverage of the bridge/roadway; a full generative model (HunyuanWorld, WorldGen-from-text, WonderWorld) would hallucinate structure that doesn't match reality — a bad tradeoff for documenting real infrastructure.

Add an OPTIONAL, off-by-default post-process 'fill pass' that targets only the known-bad regions of the existing reconstruction: sky/horizon (near-zero-parallax, noisy splats) and small occlusion shadows behind railings/girders/vegetation that no camera position saw. Implement this with WorldGen (Apache-2.0, github.com/ZiYang-xie/WorldGen) as the primary candidate — it already accepts a user-supplied equirectangular pano via its `pano_image` parameter and its low-VRAM mode (~10GB) fits the free Colab T4 (16GB). Restrict it to Apache/MIT-licensed sub-backends (DA-2 depth), not any bundled non-commercial component.

As a lighter alternative or second option for sky/hole patching specifically, evaluate SPAG4d (github.com/cedarconnor/SPAG4d, MIT core, actively committed as of June 12 2026) restricted to its DA360/DAP backends only. Explicitly avoid its SHARP 360/PaGeR (Apple CC-BY-NC-4.0) and OmniRoam/ArtiFixer3D (Adobe Research License) paths in anything Orbit Studio redistributes — those are fine for the user's own hobby run but not for a general-purpose open-source tool others might use commercially. Treat SPAG4d as a small, unreviewed one-person repo (~215 stars) — useful because it's a near-exact fit, not because it's battle-tested.

Do NOT vendor or bundle Tencent HunyuanWorld 1.0/1.1(WorldMirror)/2.0 weights or code into anything Orbit Studio ships. Their 'Community License' explicitly excludes the EU, UK, and South Korea as usable territory and caps free use at 1,000,000 MAU before requiring a separate grant from Tencent — incompatible with an unrestricted open-source redistribution goal. If offered at all, document it as a manual, clearly-labeled opt-in Colab cell (same pattern the pipeline already uses for swappable components like Brush), never a default.

Skip DreamScene360 for anything beyond the user's own private/research use — it directly accepts a real user-supplied equirectangular panorama (exact input format match) but its 3D Gaussian Splatting codebase inherits the original Inria/MPII 'research purposes only' non-commercial license, so it cannot be repackaged into a tool others might use commercially.

Do not pursue Genie-3-adjacent video world models (Matrix-Game 3.0, LingBot-World) for this pipeline at all right now, regardless of their permissive licenses (LingBot-World is Apache-2.0). They generate frame-by-frame action-conditioned video, not a static exportable mesh/splat file, which is architecturally incompatible with Orbit Studio's 'bake once, host a static .splat, view in Spark/three.js' design — adopting one would mean running a live generative backend per viewing session instead of shipping a file.

Separately (not generative fill, but worth a follow-up investigation outside this slice): HunyuanWorld-Mirror / WorldMirror is a feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction model (predicts point clouds, depth, normals, camera poses in one pass, no iterative optimization) that could be evaluated as a faster alternative or complement to pycolmap for the 20-photo pose-estimation step itself — confirm its license separately before use, as it likely inherits the same Tencent Community License family.

World Labs Marble (and the MIT-licensed 'image-blaster' glue project around it) is the most polished single/few-image-to-explorable-world product on the market (World API launched Jan 21 2026, accepts panoramas) but is fully closed-weight and gated behind a paid API/ToS — not usable as a self-hosted component of an open-source tool; note it only for competitive awareness.
slices.slice: Generative world models turning one/few 360 panoramas into a walkable 3D scene (2025-2026)
slices.summary: The single-pano-to-world space split into two camps by mid-2026. Tencent's HunyuanWorld line (1.0, July 2025; 1.1/WorldMirror, Oct 2025; HY-World 2.0, Apr-May 2026) is the most capable, producing panorama-to-3DGS/mesh pipelines importable into Unity/Unreal, but ships under a "Community License" that excludes the EU, UK, and South Korea and caps free use at 1M MAU — disqualifying it from an unrestricted open-source tool. Apache-2.0 alternatives exist: WorldGen (ZiYang-xie) directly accepts a user's own equirectangular panorama and was actively updated through April 2026 (DA-2 depth swap, cubemap SHARP rework); LayerPano3D (SIGGRAPH 2025) is Apache-2.0 but text-prompt-only, no real-photo input. A niche hobby tool, SPAG4d, is purpose-built for exactly this task — equirect photo to 3DGS with explicit disocclusion/sky-hole filling via novel-view generation — with an MIT core but non-commercial (Apple/Adobe-licensed) high-quality backends. DreamScene360 (ECCV 2024) also takes real panoramas but inherits the original Gaussian-Splatting codebase's non-commercial research-only license. WonderWorld's license is undocumented and it needs 48GB VRAM, well beyond a free T4. recommendations: Prototype feeding the 20 leveled equirect JPGs straight into COLMAP's native spherical/equirectangular camera model (panorama_sfm CLI path, pycolmap-accessible) before building any ffmpeg cubemap-reframe step — if it registers cleanly it deletes an entire pipeline stage. Fall back to reframing only if pose quality is poor.

If reframing is still needed, follow the practitioner-consensus recipe over the current perspective-crop approach: cut each equirect still into 6 cubemap faces (or 6-8 horizontal yaw slices at ~90-110deg FOV) with ~10% face-to-face overlap, keep the zenith/up face for a bridge (trusses/girders overhead) rather than discarding it as real-estate workflows do, and mask or drop the nadir face where the tripod/operator sits instead of trying to hand-patch it.

Add a lightweight sharpness/coverage culling pass (Laplacian-variance scoring, batched by capture station) modeled on the realitystack 3DGaussianTools approach before handing frames to COLMAP -- with only 20 stations you want every reframed view that survives to be a good one, not a quantity play.

For operator/tripod removal, don't rely on manual nadir-patch compositing in Insta360 Studio; reproject to a handful of virtual perspective views per pano and run a SAM/YOLO mask pass (as Ronski's 360 Splat Pro / Stills Prep and the DIY 3DGaussianTools pipeline do), dilating masks ~15% to catch soft edges/shadows, then back-project the masks before COLMAP feature extraction.

Keep Brush as the trainer (matches the current vendored setup and the community's local-training tier alongside Nerfstudio/Postshot) since 20 panos x 6-8 reframed views is only ~120-160 images -- comfortably inside a free Colab T4 budget, no need to reach for a cloud service like Splatica/Spatial Studio/FreeGaussian that expects continuous video input rather than discrete stills.

Treat the resulting splat as a visual, not metrical, deliverable per AEC-industry guidance -- if bridge measurements matter downstream, cross-check scale/geometry against the COLMAP sparse point cloud or a known reference length rather than trusting the splat's geometry directly.

Standardize exposure/white-balance across all 20 capture stations (not just within a single continuous video) since these are discrete stills possibly taken at different times/lighting -- no strong community-documented HDR-bracketing recipe for still panos was found, so treat consistent locked exposure per station as the safer, field-tested substitute until dedicated guidance emerges.
slices.slice: Practitioner/community workflows (2026) for turning Insta360 photos/video into Gaussian splats: capture, reframe, and reconstruction recipes for small (~10-30) panorama counts
slices.summary: Two distinct community tracks exist in 2026. Track one is cloud-automatic: services (Splatica x Insta360, partnered April 2026; FreeGaussian; Splatware; Spatial Studio) accept a continuous 360 video and return a splat in hours, with universal capture advice -- lock exposure, move slowly overhead on a monopod/selfie stick, clean lenses, walk overlapping loops -- but none of these documented a stills-only (20-photo) input path; they are built around video. Track two is the DIY/local pipeline closer to Orbit Studio's existing design: equirectangular frames are reprojected into multiple perspective/cubemap views (6 cubemap faces with ~10% overlap is the most-cited split, per Mikhail Mokrushin's workflow writeup) because COLMAP historically could not consume spherical images directly -- Jonathan Stephens' tutorial calls horizontal-slicing "the EASIEST but not the BEST way" for exactly this reason. That constraint changed: COLMAP's panorama_sfm path added native spherical/equirectangular camera models plus a much faster GPU bundle-adjustment backend (Caspar), removing the crop/re-stitch step entirely for practitioners willing to use the CLI (not yet exposed in the GUI, confirmed via COLMAP issue #3595) -- though the exact release version/date could not be pinned down with confidence (sources conflict on 2024 vs 2026). Nadir/operator handling has shifted from manual "nadir patch" compositing toward automated masking: a solo developer's "3DGaussianTools" (realitystack Substack, May 2026) reprojects each pano to 18 virtual cameras, runs YOLO+SAM masking, and dilates masks ~15% to remove tripod/selfie-stick/shadow artifacts before training in Nerfstudio or LichtFeld Studio. A cluster of small paid Windows utilities (360 Splat Pro, 360 Video Stills Prep Tool, Metashape-to-COLMAP converter) and one open-source single-panorama tool (SPAG4d, MIT core) round out the tooling, but none specifically report results on ~10-30 discrete panorama stills of a static structure like a bridge -- that remains the least-covered scenario in current community writeups.
uncertainties: Exact COLMAP version/date for native spherical camera model + Caspar GPU bundle adjustment is unclear -- one fetch of the same release notes returned June 2024 dates, another returned June 2026; the feature's existence (panorama_sfm converting perspective back to equirectangular, Caspar as a faster alternative to Ceres) is corroborated across two independent pages but the date/version numbers conflict and should be verified directly against the colmap/colmap GitHub tags before citing a specific version.

No practitioner report was found describing the exact scenario in the prompt -- ~20 discrete leveled equirectangular STILL photos (not video) of a single static structure processed end to end into a splat. All concrete numeric workflow reports found (frame counts, splat counts, training times) are video-frame-extraction based (e.g., 6000 frames down to 40, or a 2-minute walk), so the small-still-count case is an extrapolation from the video-based recipes plus classic multi-station photogrammetry logic, not a directly cited case.

No specific community guidance was found on HDR bracketing for Insta360 still panos feeding a splat pipeline; the SeHDR paper on 3D Gaussian HDR bracketing is academic research (arXiv 2509.20400), not a documented field workflow, so the HDR-bracketing pitfall named in the task brief is not confirmed as an actual practitioner concern in current write-ups.

Whether Brush (ArthurBrussee/brush) has shipped any 2026 releases or 360/panorama-specific features could not be confirmed -- the GitHub releases page fetch returned only tagged releases through v0.3.0 (Sept 2024) with no 2026 entries, which may undercount ongoing untagged commit activity rather than reflect the project being stale.
Whether COLMAP's native spherical camera model is usable via pycolmap (Orbit Studio's current binding) rather than only the C++ CLI/panorama_sfm example script was not directly confirmed.

recommendations: Upgrade the Colab COLMAP step to COLMAP >=4.0.0 (ideally 4.1.1, released 2026-07-17) instead of hand-installing a separate GLOMAP binary — GLOMAP's own repo (github.com/colmap/glomap) was archived/deprecated on 2026-03-09 with the note it is 'fully migrated to COLMAP, where GLOMAP functionality is exposed as the global mapper'. Drop any GLOMAP-specific install step from the pipeline and just call COLMAP's `--Mapper.ba_global_use_pba`/global mapper mode.

Keep (don't remove) the existing ffmpeg perspective-reframe/cubemap-split step for the still-photo path. COLMAP 4.1.0's new native spherical/equirectangular camera model is explicitly documented as 'generally faster but less accurate than rendering perspective views' — wrong tradeoff when you only have 20 sparse stills and need every match to count, especially around thin bridge railings/trusses that suffer at equirect poles.

For splitting each of the 20 equirectangular JPGs, adopt the nerfstudio ns-process-data convention rather than a plain 6-face 90° cube: 8 faces at 120° FOV or 14 faces at 110° FOV, at pitches [-45,0,45]. This produces ~160-280 well-overlapping perspective frames from 20 panoramas, giving COLMAP's exhaustive matcher enough shared coverage to close the loop around the bridge and roadway. Use `ns-process-data images --camera-type equirectangular --images-per-equirect 14` directly, or the underlying py360convert library (pip install py360convert) if you want the split step to stay inside Orbit Studio's own scripts rather than depend on nerfstudio.

Switch feature extraction/matching in the Colab step to COLMAP's built-in ALIKED (via ONNX) + LightGlue (via ONNX) path, added natively in COLMAP 4.0.0 (2026-03-14) — this removes the need to vendor the separate hloc toolbox (whose last tagged release, v1.4, is from July 2024; ALIKED/XFeat support lives only on hloc's unreleased master via open PRs like #441). Keep classic SIFT + exhaustive matching as an automatic fallback if ALIKED/LightGlue produce a broken/disconnected reconstruction on the repetitive pavement/asphalt texture around the bridge.

Do not add OpenMVG or SphereSfM (json87/SphereSfM) to the pipeline. OpenMVG's 'Spherical' camera is reported by its own maintainers as not true equirectangular projection, with the correct model (Spherical_Equirectangular) still an open, unresolved GitHub issue (#1045) after years. SphereSfM is a maintained but niche COLMAP fork (last release 2025-08-18) that adds deployment risk versus mainline COLMAP now shipping native spherical support directly.

After matching, run COLMAP's integrated global mapper (ex-GLOMAP) first for speed, but keep the incremental mapper as an automatic retry path if global mapper output looks degenerate — GLOMAP's own paper and COLMAP's rotation-averaging robustification notes (4.1.0 changelog: 'Robustified gravity-aligned rotation averaging against 180-degree flips') both flag global SfM's known failure mode on small/structured loop scenes, which a 20-photo bridge loop is exactly.
slices.slice: Structure-from-motion for 360 imagery in 2026 (Orbit Studio research)
slices.summary: The SfM-for-360 landscape consolidated sharply into COLMAP itself in 2026. GLOMAP, the standalone fast global-SfM pipeline, was archived on 2026-03-09 after being fully merged into COLMAP 4.0.0 (2026-03-14) as a first-class 'global mapper' mode, alongside natively integrated ALIKED (via ONNX) feature extraction and LightGlue (via ONNX) matching for both SIFT and ALIKED. COLMAP 4.1.0 (2026-06-26) then added native spherical/equirectangular and Enhanced Unified Camera Model (EUCM) support plus the Caspar GPU bundle-adjustment backend (1-2 orders of magnitude faster than Ceres-CUDA); 4.1.1 (2026-07-17) is the current stable point release. Critically, COLMAP's own docs describe native equirectangular reconstruction as faster but less accurate than the classic cubemap/perspective-split approach, so for a sparse 20-photo dataset the traditional split-then-SfM workflow remains the safer choice. Nerfstudio's ns-process-data (`--camera-type equirectangular --images-per-equirect 8|14`, FOV 120deg/110deg with pitch bounds [-45,0,45]) is the closest thing to a standardized, actively-maintained splitting tool, and its main equirect artifact bug (issue #3445) is closed. hloc, by contrast, hasn't cut a tagged release since v1.4 (July 2024); its ALIKED/XFeat support lives on an unreleased master branch, making COLMAP's own native ALIKED+LightGlue integration the more current path. OpenMVG's spherical camera model is widely reported as not truly equirectangular and unresolved for years; SphereSfM (json87) is a maintained but niche research fork (last release 2025-08-18). Net: COLMAP 4.1.x alone, fed cubemap-split stills, is now the most reliable open-source pose-recovery path.

slices.slice: Sparse-view / few-shot Gaussian splatting (~10-30 camera stations): InstantSplat lineage, depth-prior regularization, 2025-2026 few-shot 3DGS papers, and the 360-photo-to-cubemap angle
slices.summary: Sparse-view 3DGS has moved fast over the last year along two axes relevant to a 20-station bridge shoot. First, pose/init: classical COLMAP struggles when only ~20 widely-spaced stations exist, so the field has shifted to feed-forward pointmap networks (DUSt3R -> MASt3R -> VGGT -> pi3) that jointly predict poses+depth+points and explicitly target "sparse and low-overlap" capture — exactly this use case; VGGT's code became commercial-use-friendly (excluding military) on 2025-07-29. Second, regularization: since InstantSplat (2024) established DUSt3R-init plus fast optimization for sparse views, a wave of 2025-2026 papers (FSGS, DNGaussian, CoR-GS, SparseGS, MS-GS, Pi-GS, DropAnSH-GS, SaveWildGS) converged on a shared recipe — monocular-depth-prior losses (Pearson correlation, not raw L2), pseudo/virtual-view interpolation between real cameras, and anchor-cluster or spherical-harmonic-coefficient dropout — to fight the two dominant failure modes: near-camera floaters and view-overfitting, rather than relying on plain opacity-reset. Pi-GS (Feb 2026) beats InstantSplat/FSGS/DNGaussian on Tanks&Temples 3-view and also reports MipNeRF360 12/24-view outdoor results. A separate but directly relevant line handles 360/panoramic captures natively: ODGS and Splatter-360 do spherical-domain (cubemap or ERP) rasterization instead of independent perspective crops, and PanoImager/LighthouseGS explicitly flag that sparse panoramic stations degrade cross-view consistency and extrapolation. No paper tests exactly "20 outdoor bridge panoramas," but MS-GS and SaveWildGS (in-the-wild, distractors, appearance variation across sessions) and Seam360GS (dual-fisheye seam/distortion calibration) each match a specific real-world hazard this shoot will hit: traffic/pedestrian ghosting, lighting drift between stations, and stitching seams. A practical (non-peer-reviewed) blog independently converged on splitting each 360 frame into 18 perspective views (a ring of 16 plus 2 poles) rather than a plain 6-face cubemap, precisely to answer the "many perspective views per panorama" question.

sources.title: I Built My Own Tools to Turn 360° Footage Into Clean Gaussian Splatting Data
key_claims: Practitioner tool (3DGaussianTools) projects each 360 frame onto 18 virtual perspective cameras — 16 in a ring (8 yaw angles x 2 pitch levels at +/-35 degrees) plus 2 polar (zenith/nadir) cameras — instead of a plain 6-face cubemap, specifically to avoid pole distortion and enable per-view object detection/segmentation.

Runs YOLO + SAM per perspective view to mask transient objects (people, selfie sticks), reprojects masks back to equirectangular space, and dilates masks ~15% to fully cover fringes (hair, shadow, motion blur) before training.
Exports either a COLMAP-style dataset (cropped cubemap faces) or a Nerfstudio-style transforms.json.

sources.title: Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction: Recent Advances and Open Challenges
key_claims: Survey covering explicit point-cloud-based approaches including 3D Gaussian Splatting, framing geometric regularization, explicit shape modeling, and generative inference as the three main strategies against floaters and pose ambiguities in sparse-view reconstruction.
quotes: floaters and pose ambiguities

recommendations: Swap (or augment) the pycolmap/COLMAP pose-estimation stage for a feed-forward pointmap network — VGGT or the lighter pi3/DUSt3R/MASt3R family — since these are explicitly built for the 'sparse and low-overlap' regime that 20 widely-spaced bridge stations will produce, where classical incremental SfM feature-matching is most likely to fail or drop stations.

When exploding each equirectangular JPG into perspective crops for reconstruction, use a ~18-view ring (e.g. 8 yaw angles x 2 pitch bands around +/-35 degrees, plus zenith/nadir) rather than a plain 6-face cubemap — this is the specific technique a practitioner (3DGaussianTools/realitystack blog) converged on for exactly this conversion, and it avoids the pole-distortion and low-parallax-density problems of a bare 6-face split.

Add a monocular-depth regularization loss (Pearson-correlation style against a pretrained depth model such as Depth Anything v2, as used in DNGaussian/MS-GS/Pi-GS) to the gsplat training loop — this is the single most consistently-reported fix across 2025-2026 few-shot 3DGS papers for the floater/overfitting failure mode that ~20 stations will trigger, and is a modest addition to an existing training loop rather than a new architecture.

Replace or supplement plain opacity-reset with an anchor/cluster-based Gaussian dropout regularizer (DropAnSH-GS) or utilization-based pruning during training — plain opacity reset is documented as weaker at cleaning outdoor floaters because dropped Gaussians get 'neighbor compensated' by nearby ones.

Plan for transient-object masking per perspective crop (traffic, pedestrians, parked vehicles) before photometric loss, mirroring the YOLO+SAM-then-dilate-then-reproject workflow in the practical blog and the distractor-handling in MS-GS/SaveWildGS — a bridge-and-roadway scene captured across ~20 separate stations is very likely to include moving vehicles in at least some frames.

If the 20 stations were shot at different times of day or in variable light (common for an outdoor multi-stop bridge survey), consider a lightweight per-image appearance embedding (MS-GS's approach) rather than assuming globally consistent exposure/white balance across stations.

Treat native panorama-domain training (ODGS-style cubemap rasterization or Splatter-360-style ERP+cubemap fusion) as a stretch goal, not a v1 requirement — it requires custom rasterizer work beyond Orbit Studio's current Spark/gsplat crop-based pipeline and should only be prototyped if the simpler perspective-crop-plus-depth-regularization approach plateaus in quality.

Budget extra floater-cleanup attention specifically for open sky and distant roadway/horizon regions — every sparse-view GS failure-mode discussion found (survey 2507.16406, TIDI-GS, DropAnSH-GS, SaveWildGS) names floaters and unbounded/far-background geometry as the primary artifact class, and a bridge-plus-roadway scene has exactly that kind of large-depth-range, sparsely-observed background.
uncertainties: The exact license terms of the NVlabs/InstantSplat repository were not confirmed beyond the presence of a LICENSE.txt file (likely a restrictive NVIDIA research license); verify before shipping it as part of an open pipeline.

Whether the 'Depth-Regularized Optimization for 3D Gaussian Splatting in Few-Shot Images' paper (arXiv 2311.13398) is the same work commonly referred to as 'DNGaussian' or a separate paper with a similar title was not fully disambiguated from search results alone.

VRAM/runtime feasibility of running VGGT or pi3 (billion-parameter-class feed-forward networks) inside a free-tier Google Colab T4 (16GB) session, as Orbit Studio's pipeline currently relies on, was not confirmed from any source found; this should be tested directly before committing to it as a COLMAP replacement.
The realitystack Substack blog post is a practitioner account, not peer-reviewed, and its exact publication date could not be confirmed beyond internal references to YOLO26/SAM3.1 suggesting 2026.

recommendations: Switch the viewer artifact format from raw .splat to Niantic's SPZ (or Spark's 'extended SPZ' with a pre-built LoD tree): Spark/three.js already auto-detects and loads .spz natively, files run ~10x smaller than PLY with 3-5x faster compression than the old SPZ, and it's MIT-licensed -- a near-zero-cost swap that speeds up load time for a bridge-scale scene in a browser on a phone.

Lean into the accuracy gap in marketing/docs: as of July 2026 no mainstream consumer tool takes a sparse set of *still* 360 photos and does metrically faithful multi-view reconstruction. Niantic Scaniverse's 360-camera pipeline explicitly rejects still equirectangular images ('Still panoramic images (.jpg, .png, etc.) are not supported' -- video (.insv/.mp4) only), and World Labs Marble's multi-image mode is admittedly generative ('combine them to generate a 3D world with elements of the real-world space'), not photogrammetric. Orbit Studio's COLMAP+gsplat pipeline from real stills is the thing neither big player ships -- position it for as-built/infrastructure documentation, not 'pretty virtual walkthrough'.

Add a same-day single-pano fallback/preview mode using the SPAG-4D approach (open-source, MIT-core, monocular-depth-to-splat, no COLMAP/poses needed, actively developed through Feb 2026) so that if COLMAP fails to register some of the 20 bridge photos (likely with wide-baseline, sparse still-panorama capture), the pipeline can still emit a rough per-panorama splat for that viewpoint instead of dropping it entirely.

Benchmark cost/turnaround messaging against the new commercial baseline: Splatica (Insta360's 3DGS partner) charges $49.95-$299.95/mo cloud processing and Niantic's own 360-camera tier is $20-$50/mo gated to video-only capture, versus Orbit Studio's free Colab T4 + open pipeline -- worth a line in the README/pitch since paid competitors just set the market's price anchor.

Treat exterior/infrastructure gaussian splatting as validated, not niche: Zillow (SkyTour, July 2025) and Apartments.com/CoStar (Matterport 3D Exteriors) both shipped exterior-focused splat viewers in the last ~12 months, and Insta360+Splatica explicitly target simulation/large-scene exports (Unity, Unreal, Isaac Sim, Omniverse) -- a bridge-and-roadway target scene is squarely in the direction the industry is already moving, reinforcing that Orbit Studio isn't solving a problem nobody has.
slices.slice: Industry/product moves Feb-Jul 2026: 360-capture-to-3D-world products (World Labs Marble, Niantic Scaniverse, Meta Horizon Hyperscape, Insta360, Matterport/Zillow/Kuula)
slices.summary: Feb-Jul 2026 was an active stretch for 360-to-3D. World Labs launched a public World API (Jan 21) and raised $1B (Feb 18), then shipped Marble 1.1/1.1 Plus (Apr 2) with auto-expanding scene coverage; but Marble's multi-image/panorama mode is explicitly generative, not metric reconstruction -- it "combines" photos to "generate" a plausible world, not a faithful digital twin. Niantic (now under John Hanke's Niantic Spatial after the Scopely game-business sale) shipped a major Scaniverse update (Apr 7) adding a paid ($20-50/mo) 360-camera-to-splat pipeline and a browser workspace for city-scale scenes -- but it hard-requires video (.insv/.mp4), explicitly rejecting still equirectangular JPGs. Niantic also open-sourced SPZ 4 (MIT), a fast compressed splat format already supported by Spark/three.js. Meta's Hyperscape Capture (Quest-only, live walkthrough capture, no photo import) is being decoupled from Horizon Worlds as Horizon goes mobile-only by June 2026. Insta360 partnered with Splatica (announced Apr 24, NAB week) to turn Insta360 X5/Antigravity A1 360 video into splats with engine exports, at $50-300/mo; a rumored Insta360 X6 is not yet shipped (expected Aug-Sept 2026). In real estate, Zillow's SkyTour (2025) and Matterport 3D Exteriors on Apartments.com/CoStar both normalized exterior gaussian splats at platform scale. A smaller open-source project, SPAG-4D (MIT core, active through Feb 2026), converts a single equirectangular still to a splat via monocular depth -- the closest thing found to a still-photo-native open tool, but single-view only, not multi-photo fusion. Net signal: the industry is racing toward splats from 360 capture, but every major shipped product wants either video frames or accepts stills only for generative (not reconstructive) output -- leaving genuine multi-still-photogrammetry, especially for outdoor infrastructure, an open lane.

slices.summary: Meshroom 2025.1.0 (released 2025-08-19, still the latest stable tag as of 2026-07-23; only nightly `develop` builds are newer) restructured AliceVision's node graph into a plugin architecture with sub-process-isolated Python nodes and spun up MeshroomHub (github.com/meshroomHub), a registry of experimental ML plugins including mrGSplat, mrDepthEstimation, MrSegmentation, and others. mrGSplat wraps nerfstudio's gsplat inside Meshroom nodes (PrepareImagesForGSPlat, GaussianSplattingOptim, GaussianSplattingRender, ConvertGSplatModel) but as of mid-2026 remains developer-preview only -- no UI installer, manual rez-env setup, 57 commits, 4 open issues, and a README admitting pose optimization underperforms. Equirectangular/spherical support in AliceVision predates this release: CameraInit gained an "equirectangular" camera-model option in Meshroom 2023.3.0 (2023-12-07), and AliceVision separately ships a split360Images tool that cube-maps panoramas into perspective sub-images for standard SfM -- functionally the same crop-and-reconstruct approach Orbit Studio's ffmpeg step already uses. Meshroom and AliceVision are both MPL-2.0 (confirmed via each repo's LICENSE-MPL2.md/COPYING.md), though optional AliceVision dependencies carry BSD, LGPL, EPL, and MIT licenses. OpenSfM (BSD-2-Clause, copyright mapillary 2014) documents a genuine, production-heritage "spherical" projection type via camera_models_overrides.json, but its own `export_colmap.py` hard-errors (`ValueError`) on spherical cameras -- it only maps brown/perspective/fisheye types to COLMAP formats -- so there is no built-in OpenSfM-to-COLMAP bridge for panorama poses. Recent 2026 OpenSfM issues (Feb/Mar/Apr) are build/dependency bugs, not spherical-model fixes; the spherical-titled issues are all from 2018-2022 and several remain unresolved, suggesting the feature is stable but effectively unmaintained.

Whether AliceVision's direct 'equirectangular' CameraInit path (vs. split360Images cropping) can actually perform full 6-DOF incremental SfM across multiple moving panorama positions, or is scoped mainly to HDRI panorama stitching/alignment, was not conclusively verified from available docs.

slices.slice: Diffusion/video-prior artifact repair and view densification for sparse-view 3DGS (Difix3D+, GSFixer, GSFix3D, VidSplat, OracleGS, GaMO)
slices.summary:
A 'generative repair' cluster for sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting has consolidated over the last year, all sharing one mechanism: a diffusion or video-diffusion model synthesizes/cleans novel-view 2D images, which are fed back as extra photometric supervision into standard 3DGS optimization -- meaning every method is a data-augmentation front-end, not a change to the splat trainer itself, so any of them can in principle sit in front of gsplat or Brush unmodified. Maturity and licensing vary sharply. NVIDIA Difix3D+ (CVPR 2025 Oral) is the most usable today: public HuggingFace weights (nvidia/difix, nvidia/difix_ref), a single-step SD-Turbo-scale model (cheap versus the rest), and a documented nerfstudio/gsplat post-processing hook -- but under NVIDIA's non-commercial research license plus a Stability AI sub-license. GSFixer (ICML 2026, GVCLab) and GSFix3D (arXiv 2508.14717) post the strongest artifact-restoration numbers (GSFixer beats Difix3D+ and GenFusion on the new DL3DV-Res benchmark) but need a 5B-parameter CogVideoX-5B video-diffusion backbone trained on H20/H100 clusters (GSFixer) or per-scene diffusion fine-tuning on a 24GB Ada card (GSFix3D) -- neither fits a free T4, and GSFixer ships no LICENSE file at all. GaMO (arXiv 2512.25073, CC BY 4.0, code public) reframes the problem as geometry-aware outpainting and is the best conceptual match for filling gaps between few outdoor viewpoints, running in ~8 min/scene on an RTX 4090, but its repo is still pre-alpha (3 conda envs, indoor-only demo). recommendations: Do not adopt PanoSplatt3R as a production path yet: the GitHub repo (zhichu99/PanoSplatt3R) has license:null in the GitHub API and no LICENSE file in the file tree -- despite full code/weights/eval/training release, there is no explicit reuse grant. Before shipping any Orbit Studio feature that depends on it, either get written permission from the authors or wait for a license file to appear.

PanoSplatt3R is strictly a 2-panorama (pairwise) model -- its own project page says 'Given two panorama images as input,' and the repo ships only pairwise relative-pose evaluation (evaluate_pose.sh), no multi-view global aligner. To use it across the user's ~20 bridge-station panoramas you would have to build your own pairwise-chaining + pose-graph fusion on top -- that is new engineering work for Orbit Studio, not a drop-in swap for COLMAP.

PanoSplatt3R's only public training/test data is HM3D and Replica, both indoor scan datasets; there is no outdoor demo, benchmark table, or sample in the repo or project page. Its ICCV paper abstract claims 'indoor and outdoor, egocentric, and roaming' generalization but that is not backed by any public outdoor artifact -- treat outdoor (bridge/roadway) performance as unverified, and prototype on 2-3 of the user's real photos before trusting it.

OmniSplat (MIT license) is the only one of the three panorama-native models with genuine outdoor training/eval data (360Roam, OmniPhotos, 360VO all include outdoor/urban scenes) -- but it is built on posed MVSplat and requires per-scene SfM poses from OpenMVG, so it is NOT pose-free like PanoSplatt3R. It also has a known, unfixed pixel-misalignment bug in equirectangular warping (documented manual patch to the pyequilib library) and an open, unanswered GitHub issue asking exactly the user's question ('How to infer on my own dataset?'). Treat as experimental only.

PanSplat (MIT license) requires >=24GB VRAM for its 4K checkpoint (RTX 3090-class) and was trained on an A100 -- it will not run on a free Colab T4, which breaks Orbit Studio's zero-cost-GPU constraint. It is also not pose-free: its real-video workflow first runs stella_vslam SLAM to recover poses before predicting Gaussians. Skip it unless the user's budget model changes to allow a paid GPU tier.

None of PanoSplatt3R/OmniSplat/PanSplat natively fuse more than 2 panoramas into one consistent scene -- this is a structural gap versus the existing perspective-split + COLMAP/pycolmap baseline (and versus MapAnything), which natively solves multi-image registration across all N inputs at once. For a 20-station bridge capture, the existing perspective-split + COLMAP path remains the only baseline with proven >2-view global fusion; keep it as the default pipeline.

Track facebookresearch/map-anything as the more promising near-term upgrade to the existing baseline, not the panorama-native models: its code is Apache-2.0, it now ships a second checkpoint tier (facebook/map-anything-apache-v1) trained only on permissively-licensed data and released under Apache-2.0 (vs. the default checkpoint's CC-BY-NC-4.0), and it has shipped four releases in 2026 alone (v1.1 Jan 18, v1.1.1 Mar 23 with Apple MPS + Pixio encoder, v1.1.2 May 30 with VGGT Omega, v1.1.3 Jul 17). It still has no documented equirectangular/panorama ingestion in its own README, so Orbit Studio would still need the perspective-split step -- but swapping the fully-open Apache checkpoint in for COLMAP/pycolmap where feasible is a lower-risk, license-clean improvement than adopting any of the three direct-panorama models today.

Revisit this slice in ~6 months: PanoSplatt3R, OmniSplat, and PanSplat have all been dormant (no commits) since Oct 2025 (PanoSplatt3R), Jun 2025 (OmniSplat), and Apr 2026-copyright-only (PanSplat) respectively -- none show February-July 2026 feature development, so the pose-free direct-panorama family is not yet moving fast enough to justify a pipeline rewrite; MapAnything is the actively-developed piece worth re-checking sooner.
slices.slice: Panorama-native pose-free reconstruction: PanoSplatt3R (ICCV 2025) and the OmniSplat/PanSplat family
slices.summary:
PanoSplatt3R (github.com/zhichu99/PanoSplatt3R, arXiv 2507.21960, ICCV 2025) is fully code-and-weights released: its TODO checklist (Evaluation Code, Training Code, Model Checkpoint, Test Dataset) is entirely checked, with weights hosted on HuggingFace (zhichu99/PanoSplatt3R). However, the GitHub API reports license:null and no LICENSE file exists in the repo -- it is publicly visible but not explicitly open-sourced. It is strictly a 2-panorama (pairwise), pose-free model built on a MASt3R/DUSt3R-style ViT backbone with a novel "RoPE rolling" position encoding for horizontal panorama periodicity; it ships no >2-view global-alignment tool. Its only public training/test datasets are HM3D and Replica (both indoor); no outdoor demo or benchmark is shown despite the paper's abstract claiming indoor/outdoor generalization. Training needs >=48GB VRAM (NVIDIA L40 used); inference-specific VRAM is undocumented anywhere in the repo, paper, or project page. The repo has been dormant since Oct 17, 2025 (last push), with open unresolved issues about custom/unposed inference.

OmniSplat (github.com/esw0116/OmniSplat, arXiv 2412.16604, CVPR 2025 Highlight) is MIT-licensed and, notably, is the only one of the three with genuine outdoor training/eval coverage (360Roam, OmniPhotos, OmniBlender/Ricoh360, OmniScenes, 360VO). But it is not pose-free -- it runs on posed MVSplat and requires OpenMVG-derived SfM poses per scene -- and carries a known, unpatched equirectangular pixel-misalignment bug plus an unanswered "how do I use my own data" issue. Dormant since June 6, 2025.

PanSplat (github.com/chengzhag/PanSplat, arXiv 2412.12096, CVPR 2025) is MIT-licensed, actively maintained into 2026 (commits through Apr 19, 2026, though recent ones are minor/cosmetic), and offers downloadable checkpoints up to 4K (2048x4096) -- but the 4K model needs >=24GB VRAM (RTX 3090-class, trained on A100), ruling out a free T4. It is also not pose-free (real-video pipeline relies on stella_vslam SLAM poses). Training data is indoor-dominant (Matterport3D/Replica/Residential) with 360Loc real-world fine-tuning data that does include outdoor urban/park scenes.

As a baseline comparison, facebookresearch/map-anything (Apache-2.0 code) is far more active in this window (four 2026 releases through Jul 17, 2026) and now offers a fully Apache-2.0 checkpoint tier (map-anything-apache-v1) alongside its default CC-BY-NC-4.0 weights -- but it has no native panorama/equirectangular input, so the perspective-split step Orbit Studio already uses remains necessary.

recommendations: Do not swap pycolmap out yet: none of the direct-equirect papers use COLMAP for pose recovery (it has no spherical/equirectangular camera model) — they use OpenMVG (OmniGS, ODGS) or OpenSfM (the hobby recipe below). Adopting direct-equirect training means also replacing the SfM stage, which is a bigger, riskier pipeline change than it first appears for only 20 outdoor stills.

If you want to prototype direct-from-equirect training, start from esw0116/ODGS (MIT, NeurIPS 2024) rather than OmniGS (GPL-3.0, heavier CUDA/LibTorch/OpenCV-CUDA native build) — ODGS is Python/PyTorch-ish, permissively licensed, and closer to your existing gsplat/Brush stack, but expect a stale repo (no commits since Dec 2024) and the need to wire in OpenMVG for poses yourself.

Treat SC-OmniGS, Spherical-GOF, ErpGS, and TPGS as watch-only for now: each claims strong outdoor or pose-free results but has no runnable public training code as of July 2026 (SC-OmniGS repo is a project webpage only; Spherical-GOF repo has just README+LICENSE with code 'will be released'; ErpGS project page literally says 'Code (Coming Soon)'; TPGS repo has 17 commits but an incomplete README with no working setup instructions).

Skip the feed-forward pair methods (PanSplat, Splatter-360, OmniSplat) for this goal — they solve 2-view interpolation/generalization, not fusing ~20 wide-baseline stills into one consistent walkable scene, and are validated mainly on indoor synthetic benchmarks (Matterport3D, HM3D, Replica). PanSplat's Insta360-video fine-tune is the most real-world-relevant checkpoint of the three but is still pairwise, not a full-scene reconstruction from N stills.

Best low-risk experiment: keep your current pycolmap perspective-crop SfM exactly as-is (it is proven on outdoor unbounded scenes), but aggregate the recovered per-crop poses back into one pose per source equirect frame and feed that into an ODGS/OmniGS-style equirect rasterizer for the final gsplat training pass instead of the resampled perspective crops. This captures the no-crop-seam benefit of direct-equirect training without abandoning the SfM stage that already works for you.

Warn the user up front that 20 stills is sparse for a large outdoor scene (a bridge plus surrounding roadways): every panorama-GS paper surveyed here demonstrates on dozens-to-hundreds of frames or continuous video, not ~20 discrete stills. Recommend either capturing more panoramas spaced along the roadway/under the deck, or leaning on a monocular-depth prior (as LighthouseGS, ErpGS, and the hobbyist SPAG4d tool do) to regularize the sparse regions, regardless of which splat variant is ultimately used.

For a quick practical spike (not a citation-grade research contribution), inuex35/360-gaussian-splatting is the closest existing recipe to 'N equirect stills -> OpenSfM spherical poses -> panorama-aware 3DGS training' end to end, and worth cloning to see how far it gets on a bridge dataset before investing in any of the CVPR/ICLR papers above — but it is an unpublished hobby repo with unverified maintenance state, so budget time for debugging.
slices.slice: Papers/code that train 3D Gaussian Splatting directly from equirectangular/360 panoramas (no perspective-crop preprocessing) — OmniGS, 360-GS, ODGS, Splatter-360, PanSplat, OmniSplat, ErpGS, PanoGS, TPGS, and newer 2026 work
slices.summary: Direct-from-equirect 3DGS is an active but still academic-maturity field as of July 2026. Real, runnable, per-scene optimization code exists for OmniGS (WACV 2025, GPL-3.0, C++/CUDA equirect rasterizer) and ODGS (NeurIPS 2024, MIT, PyTorch) — both require poses from OpenMVG, not COLMAP, since COLMAP has no spherical camera model. 360-GS (Feb 2024) also has public code (LeoDarcy/360GS) using tangent-plane projection with a custom panorama rasterizer, indoor-focused. The self-calibrating/pose-free option that would most help a sparse-still capture, SC-OmniGS (ICLR 2025), has only a project webpage on GitHub, not training code. Newer 2026 work (Spherical-GOF, CylinderSplat, UniTriSplat, PFGS360, ODGS-SLAM) pushes geometry quality and pose-freeness further but is either code-not-yet-released, video-sequence-oriented (not discrete stills), or unverified in this research pass. ErpGS and TPGS address outdoor 360-rig distortion and single-panorama reconstruction respectively, but ErpGS's code is "coming soon" and TPGS's repo is incomplete/undocumented. Feed-forward generalizable methods (Splatter-360, PanSplat, OmniSplat) are the most code-complete and well-maintained (pretrained checkpoints, active repos), but solve 2-view interpolation for indoor synthetic benchmarks, not many-view outdoor scene fusion. SPaGS (EGSR/CGF 2025) is notable for an explicit outdoor drone-panorama dataset but ships as a plugin to a heavyweight research framework. Bottom line: perspective-split remains the practical route for Orbit Studio today, primarily because it lets you keep COLMAP for pose recovery; direct-equirect training is promising but not a drop-in replacement.

sources.title: GitHub - 1170632760/Spherical-GOF (Spherical-GOF: Geometry-Aware Panoramic Gaussian Opacity Fields for 3D Scene Reconstruction)
key_claims: Performs Gaussian Opacity Field ray sampling directly on the unit sphere rather than via projection-based rasterization, claiming 57% depth-reprojection-error reduction and 21% cycle-inlier-ratio improvement over the strongest baseline
MIT licensed, but the repo currently contains only .gitignore, LICENSE, README, and an assets folder — 2 commits total, no source implementation files
References a forthcoming 'OmniRob' dataset that is also not yet released

sources.title: GitHub - nerficg-project/SPaGS (SPaGS: Fast and Accurate 3D Gaussian Splatting for Spherical Panoramas, Computer Graphics Forum 2025)
key_claims: MIT licensed; ships as a plugin/module for the separate 'NeRFICG' research framework (installed via ./scripts/install.py -m SPaGS), not a standalone repo
Introduces exact axis-aligned bounding box calculation for spherical images to speed up omnidirectional ray casting of 3D Gaussians

Ships a new 'RaR' (Roaming and Rounding) dataset with real outdoor drone-captured scenes (named O_car, O_lion, O_statuary, O_stone, O_windmill) that pair panoramic and simultaneous perspective captures

sources.title: CylinderSplat: 3D Gaussian Splatting with Cylindrical Triplanes for Panoramic Novel View Synthesis (arXiv / ICLR 2026)
key_claims: Introduces a cylindrical Triplane representation aligned to panoramic/Manhattan-world geometry, with a dual-branch pixel + volume architecture to handle occlusions in sparse-view panoramic capture
Explicitly designed to flexibly handle a variable number of input views, from a single panorama up to multiple panoramas, which is closer to Orbit Studio's ~20-still use case than pairwise methods
Paper references code at github.com/wangqww/CylinderSplat, but actual repo contents/completeness were not independently verified in this research pass
Accepted as an ICLR 2026 conference paper

sources.title: GitHub - inuex35/360-gaussian-splatting
key_claims: Hobbyist end-to-end recipe: runs OpenSfM (bin/opensfm_run_all) with a spherical camera model on a folder of 360 photos to produce a reconstruction.json, then trains a modified 3DGS with a --panorama training flag
Explicitly chosen because COLMAP does not support the spherical/equirectangular camera model needed for direct pose recovery from 360 stills
Vendors diff-gaussian-rasterization and simple-knn submodules and offers multiple render modes including an OmniGS-style omnidirectional renderer
README recommends a smaller densify_grad_threshold (0.00002) specifically for equirectangular projections due to increased memory demands

slices.slice: Outdoor infrastructure splat quality: sky handling, appearance/exposure correction, anti-aliasing, floater pruning, transient-object masking, nadir/tripod holes, scale calibration/georeferencing
slices.summary: Since roughly late 2025, open-source 3DGS tooling has converged on a fairly standard "outdoor quality checklist" that is now mostly flag-toggles rather than custom code. gsplat's simple_trainer.py exposes app_opt (per-image appearance embedding), post_processing={bilateral_grid,ppisp} for exposure/white-balance drift, and an antialiased flag implementing Mip-Splatting's 2D/3D filter (though gsplat issue #840 shows it can delete thin high-frequency detail). StopThePop's per-ray depth sorting remains a standalone fork (r4dl/StopThePop), not merged into gsplat/nerfstudio mainline. Sky handling has moved from "just let it floater" to explicit sky masks (skyseg U-2-Net/onnx) or dedicated sky Gaussians/skyboxes (spirulae-splat's background_mode=sh, PostShot's sky sphere, the March-2026 R3GW paper). Transient-object handling for moving cars/pedestrians now has both automatic methods (SpotLessSplats' diffusion-feature+residual masking, RobustSplat's delayed-densification + scale-cascaded mask bootstrapping, ICCV 2025) and practical mask-generation tooling (YOLO/SAM2.1/SAM3.1 in stechdrive-3dgs-utils, MIT, v1.25.2 July 2026). Floater pruning has both research methods (TIDI-GS, Clean-GS, both Jan 2026 arXiv) and the de facto manual tool, SuperSplat (MIT, browser-based lasso/crop cleanup). For 360-specific capture, COLMAP 4.1.0 (June 26, 2026) added a native EQUIRECTANGULAR spherical camera model (faster but admittedly less accurate than perspective rendering per COLMAP's own notes), while SPAG-4D and stechdrive-3dgs-utils both use cubemap/pole-cap face-splitting to handle nadir/tripod holes and offer AprilTag-based metric scale calibration as an alternative to GPS EXIF, which Insta360's JPG equirect exports typically lack.

sources.title: gsplat (nerfstudio-project) - examples/simple_trainer.py

sources.title: spirulae-splat (harry7557558)
key_claims: Bilateral grid and PPISP exposure/white-balance correction both enabled by default, disabled via --model.no_use_bilateral_grid / --model.no_use_ppisp
PPISP is described as giving less color shift than the classic affine bilateral grid, trained with AdaGrad
Skybox/sky handling via --model.background_mode sh with regularization to balance sky removal vs transparency
Supports masking to either ignore regions (sky/background) or mask foreground (people/cars) via --model.apply_loss_for_mask
Three Gaussian primitive types: 3dgs (no AA), mip (Mip-Splatting anti-aliased), 3dgut (default, distortion-aware)
Licensed GPL-3.0
quotes: PPISP (default) gives less color shift

sources.title: SPAG-4D: 360 Panorama to 3D Gaussian Splats (cedarconnor/SPAG4d)
key_claims: Converts a single equirectangular panorama into a 3DGS scene via four backends: DA360, DAP, PaGeR (depth-based) and SHARP-360 (Apple's per-face Gaussian prediction model)
SHARP-360 uses pole-cap faces (looking straight down/up) to fill the holes the horizon ring leaves at nadir and zenith, with tunable seam latitude 10-60 degrees
Optional OmniRoam refinement generates novel views to fill disocclusion holes
Core is MIT licensed; PaGeR and SHARP-360 backends carry non-commercial research-only upstream model licenses
quotes: Pole-cap faces (looking straight down/up) fill the holes the horizon ring leaves at the nadir and zenith

sources.title: stechdrive/stechdrive-3dgs-utils
key_claims: Windows GUI pipeline turning 360 video/still-image sequences into scale-calibrated 3DGS training assets

Offers three mask tiers: YOLO/SAM2.1 (fast person masks), YOLO26-sem (Cityscapes classes, defaults to person+sky, extendable to vehicles/vegetation), SAM3.1 (prompt-controlled, can add missed targets like tripods or subtract false positives like signs)
AprilTag scale calibration: user enters printed tag size and IDs, tool estimates metric scale and rescales camera positions plus point cloud
Three SfM paths: import existing Metashape/RealityScan results, COLMAP cubemap rig (360 images expanded to cubemap faces), or COLMAP 4.1+ native EQUIRECTANGULAR camera model
Exports to NeRF JSON/PLY, COLMAP format, LichtFeld Studio, Postshot, and Brush-compatible cubemap datasets
Latest release v1.25.2, MIT licensed application code, 767 commits
quotes: add missed targets such as tripods or subtract false detections such as signs and logos
COLMAP's native EQUIRECTANGULAR camera model, so no forked COLMAP build is required

sources.title: SpotLessSplats: Ignoring Distractors in 3D Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: Combines pre-trained Stable Diffusion semantic features with iterative reconstruction residuals to adaptively identify transient distractor regions without manual masks
Published in ACM Transactions on Graphics 2025
Targets casual captures with moving people, animals, or changing lighting that break 3DGS's inter-frame consistency assumption

sources.title: RobustSplat: Decoupling Densification and Dynamics for Transient-Free 3DGS
key_claims: ICCV 2025 paper; delayed Gaussian growth strategy prioritizes static structure before allowing splitting/cloning, reducing overfitting to transient objects early in optimization
Scale-cascaded mask bootstrapping starts from low-resolution feature-similarity supervision for initial transient masks then refines at high resolution

sources.title: Splatfacto-W: A Nerfstudio Implementation of Gaussian Splatting for Unconstrained Photo Collections
key_claims: Integrates per-image appearance embeddings (48-dim) and per-Gaussian appearance features (72-dim) plus a spherical-harmonics background model for varying photometric appearance and transient objects
Improves PSNR by an average of 5.3 dB over vanilla 3DGS on unconstrained (multi-time-of-day) photo collections

sources.title: TIDI-GS: Floater Suppression in 3D Gaussian Splatting for Enhanced Indoor Scene Fidelity
key_claims: Floaters are defined as Gaussians spatially isolated from the dense/coherent manifolds that valid geometry forms
Composite pruning score combines spatial isolation with low opacity and low learned importance signals

sources.title: Clean-GS: Semantic Mask-Guided Pruning for 3D Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: Removes background clutter and floaters using sparse semantic masks via whitelist-based spatial filtering plus color-guided validation and outlier removal
Achieves 60-80% model compression while preserving object quality

sources.title: georeferenced_gsplat (manudelu)
key_claims: Pipeline chaining COLMAP SfM, 3D Gaussian Splatting training, and SuGaR mesh refinement, using drone-image GPS EXIF as the georeferencing anchor
Converts the COLMAP reconstruction to an ENU (East-North-Up) coordinate frame using the first image's GPS position as reference
Exports to formats compatible with Cesium Ion and Unreal Engine

recommendations: Replace the ffmpeg-frame-extraction step (irrelevant for 20 stills) with a cubemap/perspective-face split per panorama before COLMAP, rather than relying on COLMAP 4.1's new native EQUIRECTANGULAR camera model alone -- COLMAP's own 4.1.0 release notes call native spherical reconstruction 'generally faster but less accurate than rendering perspective views,' and with only 20 source stations pose accuracy matters more than speed.

Add a per-face masking pre-pass before COLMAP feature extraction: sky mask (skyseg U-2-Net/onnx, MIT) + tripod/nadir mask, fed to COLMAP via ImageReader.mask_path so no SfM features are matched on sky or the tripod blob -- directly reduces the floater count gsplat/Brush will otherwise have to prune later.

If any of the 20 panoramas show moving cars or pedestrians on the roadway, run YOLO/SAM2.1 (or SAM3.1 prompt masks) to produce ignore-region masks and pass them into gsplat's dataset `mask` field (or spirulae-splat's `apply_loss_for_mask`) during training, not just at the COLMAP stage -- this is the same approach stechdrive-3dgs-utils and RobustSplat/SpotLessSplats use to stop transient objects from becoming ghost splats.

Turn on gsplat's existing appearance-correction flags for training: `app_opt=True` (16-dim per-image embedding) and `post_processing='bilateral_grid'` or `'ppisp'` (spirulae-splat reports PPISP gives less color shift) -- this is a config change, not new code, and directly targets exposure/white-balance drift across 20 shots taken at different times of day.

A/B test gsplat's `antialiased` (Mip-Splatting) flag on the bridge scene specifically -- gsplat issue #840 documents it deleting thin high-frequency structures (bike spokes, by analogy cables/railings), which matters for a bridge's guardrails and cable geometry; don't assume anti-aliasing is a free win here.

Add an explicit scale-calibration step since 20 tripod-mounted 360 stills won't carry a GPS track the way drone footage does (Insta360 JPG equirect export typically drops GPS unless a GPX/embed option is explicitly used): either place one printed AprilTag of known size in a couple of frames (as stechdrive-3dgs-utils does) or feed COLMAP's model_aligner one or two known real-world distances (railing post spacing, lane width) as control points -- otherwise the splat is unscaled and can't be measured or georeferenced.

Add a cheap manual cleanup pass with SuperSplat (browser-based, MIT, playcanvas/supersplat) before shipping artifact.splat: crop scene bounds and lasso-remove stray sky/water floaters -- no new dependency, it's already the community-standard post-processing step.

For the nadir tripod hole in each of the 20 stations, don't attempt generative inpainting (overkill for 20 stills) -- either mask-and-accept the hole (simplest) or crop/plane-fill it in SuperSplat afterward; reserve pole-cap-with-seam-latitude techniques (SPAG-4D's approach) only if a filled floor patch under each station is actually needed for the fly-through.
uncertainties: Whether StopThePop's per-ray depth sorting has ever been merged into gsplat, nerfstudio, or any other mainline trainer -- all evidence found shows it remains a standalone reference implementation/fork (r4dl/StopThePop, r4dl/StopThePop-Rasterization); could not confirm any upstream integration.

Exact GPS/EXIF retention behavior of the Insta360 X4 Air's own equirectangular JPG export path specifically -- only general Insta360 X4 behavior was confirmed (raw .insv/GPX retains GPS, exported JPG/MP4 via software typically does not by default).
The full expansion/meaning of the 'PPISP' acronym used by gsplat and spirulae-splat as a bilateral-grid alternative was not found in any fetched source.

Moshpit360 (LichtFeld Studio plugin for one-click 360 video to 3DGS) had no confirmed release date, explicit license, or documented nadir/sky/scale-handling behavior as of the source checked -- described only as 'in the final stages of development.'

Whether the 'sky segmentation network unifying transformers with a lightweight MLP' phrasing that surfaced in search summaries refers to one specific named 2026 tool/paper or is a generic paraphrase spanning several outdoor-3DGS papers (e.g., R3GW) could not be pinned to a single primary source.

No primary source specifically benchmarked any of these techniques (bilateral grid, sky masking, transient masking, AA) on a bridge/roadway scene or on Insta360-style 360 still-photo panoramas as opposed to drone/video capture -- the bridge-specific applicability is an inference, not a directly confirmed claim.
